title: This Newt Could Kill a Roomful of People. One Snake Eats It Anyway

scenes.text: This newt can kill almost anything that swallows it. Except one snake.
The rough-skinned newt of the American Northwest carries tetrodotoxin, the pufferfish poison, in its skin. One newt can hold enough to kill ten to twenty people.
In 1979, a man in Oregon swallowed one on a dare. He died.
So why would a small newt need that much poison? Because of one neighbour: the common garter snake.
It is the only animal known to eat this newt and survive. The snakes keep getting more resistant, so only the most toxic newts live, and the next generation is deadlier still.
The snake pays too. The most resistant ones crawl more slowly. Neither side can stop.

description:
The rough-skinned newt carries enough poison to kill a roomful of people, and one snake eats it anyway.
Its skin holds tetrodotoxin; according to Stanford researchers some populations produce enough to kill thousands of mice or 10 to 20 humans, and a 29-year-old man in Oregon died in 1979 after swallowing one on a dare. Common garter snakes that live alongside the newts have evolved resistance, which in turn favours ever more toxic newts, a textbook evolutionary arms race described in PLOS Biology in 2008. The most resistant snakes crawl more slowly than the others.
Who do you think wins in the end, the newt or the snake?
subject: rough-skinned newt
first_comment: In a few places the snakes have pulled so far ahead that the newts' poison can't keep up. Who would you bet on, the newt or the snake?
